before.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

before.claim: 1.1 (The slab model.) By [L2] the set $M$ is an open submanifold of $A$ with the restricted chart $x$, and the restricted fields $g=\eta|_M$ and $N=\partial_0|_M$ are smooth; the components of $g$ in the restricted chart are the constants $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and $g(N,N)=\eta(\partial_0,\partial_0)=-1<0$, so $N$ is a time orientation of $(M,g)$ and $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold. Applying [L3] to this chart gives the vanishing of the Christoffel symbols and the curvature of the metric-selected connection and the geodesic character of coordinate curves. Since $M$ is open in $A$ and $g$ restricts $\eta$, the notions of locally absolutely continuous curve, velocity and pointwise causal character agree for curves in $M$ whether read in $(M,g)$ or in $(A,\eta)$. This proves (a).

2.1 (Monotonicity and Lipschitz bounds.) Let $u:I\to M$ be a future causal curve of $(M,g)$. By (a) it is a future causal curve of $(A,\eta)$, so [L4] applies: $x^0\circ u$ is strictly increasing and $|z(u(t'))-z(u(t))|_{\mathrm e}\le x^0(u(t'))-x^0(u(t))$ for $t<t'$ in $I$, and $x^0\circ u$ is locally absolutely continuous. This is the quantitative input used below.

2.2 (Cone characterization and convexity in the slab.) By [L1] and $g=\eta|_M$, the future cones at points of $M$ are those of the chart. Since $M$ is convex in the coordinates of $x$, the straight segment between $p,q\in M$ lies in $M$; if $q-p\in C^+$ (respectively $\overline{C^+}$) the straight path $s\mapsto p+s(q-p)$ is a future timelike (respectively causal) curve in $M$ from $p$ to $q$, so $q\in I^+_M(p)$ (respectively $q\in J^+_M(p)$). Conversely a future causal curve in $M$ is one in $A$, and [L5] gives $q-p\in\overline{C^+}$ when $q\in J^+_M(p)$; for $q\in I^+_M(p)$ the strict cone membership is the same statement with $C^+$. Finally, [L6] gives $C^++\overline{C^+}\subseteq C^+$ and $\overline{C^+}+\overline{C^+}\subseteq\overline{C^+}$.

2.3 (The vertical geodesic, its maximal domain and inextendibility.) Let $\gamma(s):=x^{-1}(s,z_0)$ for $s\in(0,1)$. Its coordinate path is $y(s)=(s,z_0)$, so $\dot y=(1,0,0,0)$ and $\ddot y=0$; by [L3] and [L8] it is a smooth geodesic with affine parameter $s$, and its tangent $\gamma'(s)=\partial_0$ satisfies $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-1<0$, so $\gamma$ is a future timelike curve. Suppose a geodesic $\tilde\gamma:(a,b)\to M$ with $a<1/2<b$ restricts to $\gamma$ on $(0,1)$ and has $b>1$. In the chart, both coordinate paths satisfy the first-order geodesic system of [L8] with the same initial data at $s=1/2$, namely $(y,\dot y)=((1/2,z_0),(1,0,0,0))$, because the Christoffel symbols vanish; by uniqueness in [L8] the coordinate paths agree on $(a,b)$, so $\tilde\gamma(s)=x^{-1}(s,z_0)$ for $s\in(1/2,b)$. But for $s\in(1,b)$ the point $(s,z_0)$ does not lie in $x(M)=(0,1)\times\mathbb R^3$, so $\tilde\gamma$ is not defined there — a contradiction. The same argument at the past end excludes $a<0$. Hence no geodesic with these data extends the parameter interval beyond $(0,1)$. If $\gamma(s)$ converged to a point $q\in M$ as $s\to1$, then continuity of the chart coordinate $x^0$ on $M$ would give $1=\lim_{s\to1}x^0(\gamma(s))=x^0(q)<1$, a contradiction; hence $\gamma$ is future-inextendible in the sense of clause (d) of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and its affine parameter is bounded above by $1$. Thus $(M,g,N)$ admits an inextendible future timelike geodesic with bounded affine domain: it is timelike geodesically incomplete. This proves (b).

3.1 (Range of an inextendible causal curve.) Let $u:I\to M$ be an inextendible causal curve (future-inextendible and past-inextendible). Suppose first that $u$ is future-inextendible, and put $T:=\sup\,(x^0\circ u)(I)\le1$, finite because $x^0<1$ on $M$. If $T<1$, then $x^0\circ u$ is increasing with limit $T$, and by the Lipschitz bound of step 2.1 the spatial curve $z\circ u$ is Cauchy as $t\to\sup I$: for $t,t'$ close to $\sup I$ one has $|z(u(t'))-z(u(t))|_{\mathrm e}\le|x^0(u(t'))-x^0(u(t))|\to0$. By [L9] it converges to some $z_\infty\in\mathbb R^3$; hence $u(t)\to q:=x^{-1}(T,z_\infty)$ as $t\to\sup I$, and $q\in M$ because $T<1$ and $T\ge0$. By [L7] the curve $u$ is then extendible past its upper end, contradicting future-inextendibility. Hence $T=1$. The past argument is the time reverse and gives $\inf\,(x^0\circ u)(I)=0$; so $x^0\circ u$ is a strictly increasing continuous function on the interval $I$ whose image has infimum $0$ and supremum $1$ and contains neither endpoint (all values lie in $(0,1)$). Therefore its image is exactly the interval $(0,1)$, and for every $c\in(0,1)$ there is exactly one $t\in I$ with $x^0(u(t))=c$: existence by surjectivity, uniqueness by strict monotonicity.

3.2 (Strong causality.) Let $p\in M$ and let $U\subseteq M$ be an open neighborhood of $p$. Choose $0<\varepsilon<\min\bigl(x^0(p),\,1-x^0(p)\bigr)$ so small that the open set $V:=\{q\in M:p-\varepsilon e_0\ll_M q\ll_M p+\varepsilon e_0\}$ is contained in $U$; this is possible because $V$ shrinks to $\{p\}$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ (in the chart it is an open double cone around $p$ intersected with $M$). By the choice of $\varepsilon$, the points $p\pm\varepsilon e_0$ lie in $M$. Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a future causal curve with $\gamma(a),\gamma(b)\in V$ and let $a<t<b$. Since $\gamma|_{[a,t]}$ and $\gamma|_{[t,b]}$ are future causal curves, step 2.2 gives $\gamma(t)-\gamma(a)\in\overline{C^+}$ and $\gamma(b)-\gamma(t)\in\overline{C^+}$; since $\gamma(a)\in V$, step 2.2 gives $\gamma(a)-(p-\varepsilon e_0)\in C^+$, and by [L6] $\gamma(t)-(p-\varepsilon e_0)=\bigl(\gamma(a)-(p-\varepsilon e_0)\bigr)+\bigl(\gamma(t)-\gamma(a)\bigr)\in C^+$. Similarly $(p+\varepsilon e_0)-\gamma(b)\in C^+$ and $(p+\varepsilon e_0)-\gamma(t)=\bigl((p+\varepsilon e_0)-\gamma(b)\bigr)+\bigl(\gamma(b)-\gamma(t)\bigr)\in C^+$. By the convexity and cone characterization of step 2.2, $p-\varepsilon e_0\ll_M\gamma(t)\ll_M p+\varepsilon e_0$, that is $\gamma(t)\in V$. Hence no future causal curve leaves $V$ and later re-enters it, and $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal.

3.3 (Compactness of the causal diamonds.) Let $p,q\in M$. By the cone characterization of step 2.2, $$J^+_M(p)\cap J^-_M(q)=\{r\in M:r-p\in\overline{C^+},\ q-r\in\overline{C^+}\}.$$ The corresponding set $K:=\{r\in\mathbb R^4:r-p\in\overline{C^+},\ q-r\in\overline{C^+}\}$ in the chart is closed (the cone is closed) and bounded with $x^0(r)\in[x^0(p),x^0(q)]\subset(0,1)$; hence $K$ is a compact subset of $\mathbb R^4$ by [L9] and, being contained in the open box $x(M)$, it is a compact subset of $x(M)\cong M$. Therefore the diamond $x^{-1}(K)=J^+_M(p)\cap J^-_M(q)$ is compact in $M$.

4.1 (The Cauchy slice.) The set $\Sigma_{1/2}=x^{-1}(\{1/2\}\times\mathbb R^3)$ is the level set of the chart coordinate $x^0$ at a regular value, hence an embedded three-dimensional submanifold with a slice chart given by $x$; its tangent space is spanned by $\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3$ with $g(\partial_i,\partial_j)=\delta_{ij}>0$, so it is spacelike. By step 3.1 every inextendible causal curve of $(M,g)$ has $x^0$-range exactly $(0,1)$ and meets the level $x^0=1/2$ in exactly one parameter value; by clause (c) of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] this says that $\Sigma_{1/2}$ is a Cauchy set, and with the first part a Cauchy hypersurface. This proves (c).

5.1 (Conclusion.) Part (a) is step 1.1, part (b) is step 2.3, part (c) is step 4.1. By steps 3.2 and 3.3 the model is strongly causal and all its causal diamonds are compact, which is global hyperbolicity in the sense of clause (c) of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]; this is (d). The same model is timelike geodesically incomplete by (b), so in this class global hyperbolicity does not imply geodesic completeness.
